title: Runtime sidecar: log replay & validator for Loki/Elastic ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight runtime sidecar and central replay service that validates structured logs at application edge, enforces correlation IDs/span anchors, and provides safe replay into both Loki and Elasticsearch. The goal is to reduce downstream noise from malformed events, recover from short-term pipeline failures, and preserve trace linkage for latency/error dashboards.
background: We currently see intermittent malformed JSON and missing correlation IDs that break downstream dashboards and complicate trace joins. Operators sometimes need to re-ingest historical events after schema fixes, and our Loki/Elastic pipelines have limited tooling for safe replays and dry-run validation. This ticket implements a validation + replay path close to the producer to catch issues earlier and provide deterministic re-ingestion.
proposed_solution: 1) Runtime sidecar (language-agnostic HTTP/gRPC proxy) that performs lightweight schema recognition, correlation ID enforcement, and optional enrichment (span_anchor mapping). 2) Buffered replay store (append-only segmented log in S3 or internal blobstore) that keeps raw events for 24-72h with metadata about validation failures. 3) Replay controller service with dry-run mode that replays validated events into Loki and Elasticsearch targets with per-tenant rate limits and idempotent dedupe keys. 4) Admin UI / CLI for running dry-runs, previewing sample payloads, and resolving malformed event classes.
design_decisions: Sidecar instead of library to avoid language SDK adoption burden and to make uptake incremental.
Validation is schema-discovery plus permissive JSON path rules; do NOT attempt full schema evolution enforcement in phase 1 to reduce latency.
Replay store retention default 48h, configurable per-tenant. Short retention reduces storage cost and encourages timely fixes.
Use idempotency key derived from tenant + event_id + timestamp window to make replay safe to run multiple times into Loki/ES.
Dry-run mode writes to a shadow Loki/es index and emits a reconciliation report rather than mutating production data by default.
Correlation ID enforcement will be opt-out per route for legacy systems; we will emit high-priority alerts for routes with >5% missing IDs.
Prefer eventual consistency and at-least-once replay semantics with explicit dedupe in the sink rather than strict exactly-once in phase 1.
Store minimal lineage metadata (producer hostname, sidecar version, validation result, failure reason code) alongside raw event for efficient triage.
Expose a small API for 'repair rules' so operators can map malformed fields to canonical shapes prior to replay.
Integrations: Loki for streaming logs (labels preserved), Elastic for full-text historical queries. Mapping layer will translate sidecar metadata into Loki labels and ES index templates.
tasks: Spec: define validation ruleset and failure taxonomy (PM+SRE)
Sidecar prototype (Go) with gRPC/HTTP front and async forward to replay store and real sink
Replay store implementation (segmented append) and retention lifecycle job
Replay controller service with dry-run and per-tenant throttling
Sink adapters: Loki adapter (push labels + stream) and Elastic adapter (bulk index + template management)
Admin UI wireframe and CLI for dry-run/playback/repair
E2E test harness: synthetic producers, fault injection, latency/load tests
Runbook and oncall dashboard + alerts for validation spike and replay errors
Security review for storing raw events (PII), KMS integration for at-rest encryption
milestones: M1: Validation spec approved and sidecar MVP (2026-02-25)
M2: Replay store + basic controller with dry-run to shadow sinks (2026-03-05)
M3: Loki + Elastic adapters + QA load tests (2026-03-12)
M4: Canary rollout for two internal services with operator UI (2026-03-20)
M5: Full rollout and runbook handoff (2026-03-31)
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar validates JSON structure and emits validation outcome in 99% of calls within <4ms median added latency.
Correlation ID rule: sidecar adds a generated correlation_id when missing and marks event with "__generated_cid=true" label, or rejects when tenant opts-in to strict enforcement.
Replay dry-run creates a reconciliation report showing at least 5 sample events per failure class and no writes to production indexes when dry-run enabled.
Idempotent replay: running the same replay job twice produces the same counts in Loki/Elastic (within a tolerance of 0.1%).
End-to-end load test: 50k EPS sustained for 10 minutes through sidecar -> replay store -> controller -> Loki adapter with no data loss and error rate <0.1%.
Security: raw-event store is encrypted at rest and access-controlled; KMS key usage logged in audit trail.
rollout_plan: Start with dry-run mode for internal services in staging. Iterate on validation rules for two teams (console, runtime). Enable per-tenant opt-in strict CID enforcement only after 2-week observation window. Gradual canary: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with rollback to bypass sidecar to original sink if error rate spike >1% or latency SLO breached.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: validation-rate-by-route, failure-reason-trend, replay-success-rate, replay-latency. Alerts: validation-failure-rate >5% sustained for 10m (P1), replay-controller-runtime-exceptions >1% (P0), shadow-sink-delta >2% between dry-run and prod (P1). Traces: sidecar emits trace span with 'validation' and 'replay' spans linked to producer trace via correlation_id.
